summary.title: Apodex 1.1: Scaling Agentic Intelligence for Complex Work

setting_and_object.category: System / model technical report (agentic model + execution stack)

details: Frontier LLMs can produce correct answers but fail at 'working capability': sustained, verifiable progress on long-horizon tasks that require stateful file/search/code interaction, plan revision, failure recovery, and delivery of inspectable artifacts.

Apodex 1.1: a general-purpose model plus execution stack whose capability is scaled along two surfaces instead of only parameters/data — Environment Scaling (diverse, high-fidelity, verifier-equipped executable file, search, and code worlds that generate training trajectories) and Agentic Coordination Scaling (decomposition, delegation, staged asynchronous result integration, and replanning trained as model behaviors, realized at runtime by 'Agent Team').

Both dimensions share one execution contract: a formal task contract (workspace, actions, transitions, observations, budgets, delivery contract, terminal verifier) implemented by the AgentOS runtime, which keeps workspace, artifact, provenance, and coordination state persistent and authoritative across tools, agents, context compaction, intervention, and partial failure.

Training converts these environment and coordination trajectories into one unified policy via SFT plus agentic RL, closed by a failure-driven loop from observed capability gaps to new tasks and environments.

Task contract E = (W, W0, q, A, T, Omega, B, D, V_D) with terminal verifier S_D = V_D(W0, W_H, tau_H); solver-visible verifiers are ordinary observations, distinct from the terminal delivery verifier.
Workspace instantiated as W_t = (files, retrieved evidence, executable state/logs, artifact index, dependency/provenance graph, runtime control state).

Three filesystem namespaces (/inputs read-only, /workspace scratch, /outputs deliverables) plus optional read-only /shares document library; single-publisher lease with an exact declared output manifest reconciled against a baseline snapshot at termination.

Run-scoped Task Board held outside the LLM context (items with owners, dependencies, resolution states) periodically re-injected after compaction and used as a finalization gate; Agent Bus exposes subagent execution lifecycle (created/queued/running/reported) separately from board resolution.
Tiered context compaction triggered by provider-reported token usage: cheap tool-observation eviction first, LLM summarization only if relief is insufficient.

Soft/hard wall-clock budgets with consolidation prompt near the soft deadline and a bounded tool-free finalization call; interruptible message queue for asynchronous user intervention that renews the wall-time budget.

Unified SFT mixture over reasoning, tools, search, files, coding, math, science/finance, professional delivery, and multi-agent coordination normalized into a common stateful interaction schema; filtering removes invalid tool interactions, inconsistent state, ignored observations, incomplete delivery; rejection sampling with gold answers and per-dimension rubric thresholds otherwise; domain-specialist SFT variants merged by model soup.

RL uses PIVOT-RL: hindsight analysis identifies 'pivot' decision points (unproductive strategy, insufficient evidence, tool misuse, unrevised assumption), preserves the useful prefix, restores executable environment state, and creates localized continuation tasks with a short corrective hint (never a prediction target, absent at inference), mixed with unhinted full tasks; asynchronous rollout ingestion for heterogeneous episode costs.
Apodex 1.1 flagship (397B referenced in HDS6 analysis) and Apodex 1.1 mini at 35B parameters; predecessor Apodex 1.0 as internal reference.
Two evaluated modes: minimal ReAct scaffold (isolates the model policy) and Agent Team (dynamic subagent spawning, parallel/specialized work, focused verification).

Public: APEX-Agents, GDPVal (win rate), FrontierFinance (rubric qualification rate over 220 queries), YC-Bench, FrontierScience-Research (60 tasks, pass at >=7/10 rubric points), BioMysteryBench Human-difficult set, HLE, DeepSearchQA (F1), MathArena IMO 2025/2026 and USAMO 2026, IMO-ProofBench, Terminal-Bench 2.1, SWE-bench Verified.

Internal: FrontierSearchBench (41 verifiable deep-search tasks, per-task score in [-1,1] with penalties for wrong assertions, aggregated on a 100-point scale) and FrontierResearchBench (97 executable Docker scientific workflows graded by per-task Graders on files, numbers, formats, cross-artifact consistency; metric is full-score Pass Rate).

HDS6 process-verification framework: six process capabilities x four rubric items (0/1/2 bands), outcome-blind agentic judging over a stitched multi-agent log with citation re-grounding and an integrity gate that zeroes fabricated actions.
Baselines include Claude Opus 5 / Fable 5, GPT-5.5/5.6, Gemini 3.x, Kimi K2.6/K3, DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash, GLM-5.2, Grok-4.6, with several results reproduced under the Apodex harness.

key_findings.finding: Trained multi-agent coordination (Agent Team) yields consistent, sizable gains over the same model in a plain ReAct loop across every task family evaluated.
key_findings.evidence: ReAct to Agent Team: GDPVal 69.5 to 78.8, APEX-Agents 34.4 to 38.5, FrontierFinance 48.7 to 54.3, FrontierScience-Research 55.0 to 63.3, BioMysteryBench 23.5 to 35.3, HLE 53.2 to 56.1, DeepSearchQA 88.2 to 92.4 F1, and FrontierSearchBench 57.0 to 69.1 with the zero-credit task share roughly halved (19.5% to 9.8%).

key_findings.finding: Apodex 1.1 with Agent Team attains the top reported values in its finance, science-research, and internal deep-search comparisons while remaining behind the strongest systems on coding and hard bioinformatics.
key_findings.evidence: Best-in-table on FrontierFinance (54.3 vs 49.2 for Claude-Fable-5) and FrontierScience-Research (63.3 vs 55.0 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash) and FrontierSearchBench (69.1 vs 67.4 for GPT-5.6-Sol); but Terminal-Bench 2.1 70.8 vs 91.9 for Gemini 3.6 Flash, SWE-bench Verified 77.7 vs 92.2 for Claude Opus 5, and BioMysteryBench 35.3 vs 49.4.

key_findings.finding: The two scaling dimensions transfer to a compact 35B model, which reaches a frontier-band performance range and improves markedly over the previous mini generation.
key_findings.evidence: Apodex 1.1 mini w/ ReAct: FrontierFinance 40.0 (from 33.2 for 1.0 mini), APEX-Agents 24.2 (from 15.4), FrontierScience-Research 45.0; Agent Team lifts these by 10.2, 3.5, and 6.7 points to 50.2, 27.7, and 51.7, leading the selected FrontierFinance comparison rows.

key_findings.finding: Coordinated execution pushes competition mathematics past stated gold-medal-level reference thresholds without search.
key_findings.evidence: Agent Team scores 36.5 on IMO 2025 (threshold 35), 30.5 on IMO 2026 (29), and 26.5 on USAMO 2026 (25) under the MathArena protocol, versus ReAct 24.3/18.5/16.0 and Apodex 1.0 Agent Team 12.5/13.0/5.8; IMO-ProofBench 96.7 Basic and 63.3 Advanced versus 80.0 and 46.4 for ReAct.

key_findings.finding: Fully specified end-to-end scientific workflow delivery remains an unsolved bottleneck for all current systems, not just Apodex.
key_findings.evidence: On FrontierResearchBench (97 executable tasks requiring mutually consistent code, data, figures, and reports, scored by strict per-task Graders), the best systems reach only 20.6% Pass Rate (GPT-5.6-Sol/Codex and Grok-4.6/Claude Code), with Apodex 1.1 Agent Team at 12.4% and Apodex 1.1 under Claude Code at 10.3%.
